findings.message: Metacritic user rating count misstated in body
findings.details: Article text: "the PS5 version also carries a user score of 8.7 from 631 ratings." The metacritic.com snapshot (source-3.html.gz) states "Based on 633 User Ratings" in three places (the summary widget, the Metascore/User score panel, and the "See All 633 User Reviews" link). The 8.7 score is correct; the 631 rating count is not supported by the archived snapshot and should read 633.

content_preview.title: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced Tops 100,000 Concurrent Steam Players, a First for the Franchise
content_preview.summary: Ubisoft's remake hit a 104,756-player Steam peak three days after its 2-million-copy launch, breaking every prior Assassin's Creed concurrency record.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced has become the first game in Ubisoft's long-running franchise to draw more than 100,000 concurrent players on Steam, reaching a peak of 104,756 players three days after its July 9 launch, [according to GamesRadar+](https://www.gamesradar.com/games/assassin-s-creed/assassins-creed-black-flag-resynced-is-the-first-assassins-creed-game-ever-to-hit-over-100-000-concurrent-players-on-steam-and-it-only-took-3-days/). editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-structured News-category piece (584 words, within the 400-1200 range). Standard Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Context format. Neutral tone throughout, no editorializing or sensationalism, no AI self-reference. editor_notes.source_verification: Personally decompressed and read all 5 archived snapshots in sources/2026-07/assassins-creed-black-flag-resynced-tops-100000-concurrent-steam-players-a-first-for-the-franchise/ (source-0 through source-4, all status_code 200). Verified sha256 of each decompressed file matches manifest.json before reading. source-0 (news.ubisoft.com): confirms 2M day-one sales, #1 on Twitch July 9, 99,451 24-hour Steam concurrency peak described as the highest ever for an AC title, platform availability (PS5/Xbox Series X|S/PC via Ubisoft Store, Steam, Epic, Ubisoft+), and the Martin Schelling quote verbatim (the article merges two source sentences that were split by a mid-quote attribution in the original -- text itself is reproduced exactly, this is standard journalistic practice, not a fabrication). source-1 (gamesradar.com): confirms the 104,756 three-day concurrent peak, 'first AC game ever to hit over 100,000 concurrent players on Steam,' and every comparison figure cited (AC Shadows 64,825; AC Odyssey 62,069; AC Origins 41,551; original 2013 Black Flag 16,049); the article's 'surpassed... by more than 39,000' claim checks out arithmetically (104,756-64,825=39,931). source-2 (opencritic.com): confirms 86 Top Critic Average, 94% Critics Recommend, 160 Critic Reviews -- all exact matches. source-3 (metacritic.com): confirms 84 Metascore on PC (47 critic reviews) and PS5 (89 critic reviews), 82 on Xbox Series X (12 critic reviews), and an 8.7 user score -- but the snapshot shows 'Based on 633 User Ratings' (three separate occurrences), not the 631 stated in the article body. Flagged as a finding; see Factual Accuracy finding above. source-4 (thesixthaxis.com): confirms the Anvil-engine rebuild with ray-traced lighting, removal of the modern-day framing sequences, and roughly six extra hours of missions/story, all near-verbatim to the source text. The article's claim that TheSixthAxis scored the game 8/10 is not extractable as plain text from source-4's snapshot (likely rendered via a score widget) but is independently corroborated by the OpenCritic snapshot (source-2), which lists 'TheSixthAxis 8/10' in its aggregated critic-review table. Internal context link to the April 23, 2026 MachineHerald article on the reveal was verified to exist at src/content/articles/2026-04/23-ubisoft-confirms-assassins-creed-black-flag-resynced-reveal-for-april-23-after-trailer-leaks-three-days-early.md and its content (trailer leak, reveal event) matches the article's characterization. The 'backdrop of cost-cutting at Ubisoft, including studio closures and layoffs' context sentence has no inline citation but is corroborated by prior MachineHerald reporting (2026-02/14 article on a Ubisoft strike over studio closures, cancellations, and RTO mandate) and is standard, uncontested industry background rather than a specific disputed claim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All major figures (2M day-one sales, 99,451 24h peak, 104,756 three-day peak, franchise comparison figures, OpenCritic 86/94%/160, Metacritic 84/84/82 by platform with correct review counts, Anvil engine/ray-tracing/six extra hours) verified verbatim against source snapshots. One subordinate numeric error found: the article states the PS5 Metacritic user score is based on '631 ratings' where the archived snapshot shows 633. This is a minor, non-headline, non-lead specific -- the score itself (8.7) is correct, only the rating count is off by 2.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Attribution is consistently clear ('according to GamesRadar+', 'Ubisoft said', 'TheSixthAxis reported'). No unsupported superlatives beyond what sources state.

The only related prior coverage is the April 23, 2026 reveal-confirmation article, which this piece correctly cross-references as background context rather than duplicating.

concerns: Metacritic user rating count stated as 631 in the article body; the archived source snapshot shows 633 (score of 8.7 itself is correct). Filed as a corrections record rather than blocking publication, since it is a single subordinate specific and does not affect the headline, summary, or lead.

Three of five sources (news.ubisoft.com, opencritic.com, thesixthaxis.com) are not on config/source_allowlist.txt. Judged editorially acceptable and not treated as grounds for APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS on its own, consistent with prior review precedent (e.g. 2026-07-14 Intrinsic review, 2026-07-10 Echoes of Aincrad review): news.ubisoft.com is the subject company's own official newsroom and is the correct primary source for its own sales/quote claims; opencritic.com is a mainstream review-aggregation site directly comparable to the already-allowlisted metacritic.com; thesixthaxis.com is an established UK games outlet whose review is independently corroborated by its OpenCritic listing. Recommend the maintainers add these three domains to config/source_allowlist.txt.

One minor subordinate numeric slip (Metacritic user rating count, 631 stated vs. 633 confirmed) warrants a public corrections note but does not undermine the headline, summary, or lead, all of which are solidly sourced (104,756 peak / 100,000-player franchise first / 2-million-copy launch all confirmed verbatim).
